source.title: The Chain Rule (OpenStax Calculus Volume 1, section 3.6)
source.text:
Let f and g be functions. For all x in the domain of g for which g is differentiable at x and f is differentiable at g(x), the derivative of the composite function h(x) = (f∘g)(x) = f(g(x)) is given by h′(x) = f′(g(x))g′(x). If y is a function of u, and u is a function of x, then dy/dx = dy/du · du/dx.

To differentiate h(x) = f(g(x)), begin by identifying f(x) and g(x). Find f′(x) and evaluate it at g(x) to obtain f′(g(x)). Find g′(x). Write h′(x) = f′(g(x)) · g′(x).

For all values of x for which the derivative is defined, if h(x) = (g(x))^n, then h′(x) = n(g(x))^(n−1) g′(x).
